predecessor.description: The stack this one replaces, measured once by hand on hardware that no longer exists. Never gated against: a comparison would be between two machines as much as between two implementations. It is committed because the rebuild is accountable to it.

detect.face.on-robot.note: face pass on the robot, the original arrangement before offloading. No benchmark here produces it: this architecture has no on-robot detection path

detect.face.threads.1.note: the thread-count curve at one thread

detect.face.threads.4.note: face pass off the robot, inference runtime at four threads. This is the figure the YuNet model change has to defend

detect.face.threads.6.note: the thread-count curve at six threads, which is where it turned back upwards

footprint.image.cpu.linux-amd64.note: recorded as '483 MB' against roughly 2 GB for the alternative packaging. The unit convention was not stated; on either reading this build's image is smaller

footprint.resident_memory.note: the robot application's resident set, with no training framework ever imported. What this suite measures is the groundstation, which is where this architecture puts the model runtime, so the two are recorded beside each other rather than compared

photon-to-head.stimulus_to_motion.note: recorded as a 150-250 ms range end to end; 200 is its midpoint, and the range is what a comparison should be read against

pipeline.capability.gesture.note: gesture pass, sampled every fourth frame. This build wires no gesture model, so nothing here measures it and there is deliberately no counterpart

robot-load.cpu_cores.note: of four cores, while tracking at 10 frames per second with detection offloaded

session.connect.note: a cold connection to the robot at p50, over the same WLAN. This is the measurement that drove the robot-link design

session.round_trip.note: result delivery per request, with connection reuse enabled, over a 2.4 GHz WLAN at 100-170 ms idle round-trip

linux-x86_64-32c.description: AMD Ryzen 9 7945HX3D, 32 logical processors, 128 GiB, Linux 6.18. Figures are the median of ten consecutive runs on an idle machine; each note records the worst deviation any single run showed, which is what the tolerances are argued from.

detect.face.threads.1.note: median of ten consecutive runs on an idle host, where the worst single run deviated 4.3% from it; an eleventh run taken while the machine was also running the test suite deviated up to 77%, which is what the millisecond tolerance is set from
